name: KryptonDB
target_user: Embedded systems engineers and local-first application developers
problem: Embedded key-value stores lack native multi-document ACID transactions and rich query capabilities without pulling in bloated relational engines.
pain: Developers building local offline-first apps must choose between fragile flat files or heavy external database servers.
solution: A zero-dependency embedded document database engine written in Java 21 featuring a custom JSON-like query parser, a B+Tree on-disk index manager, multi-version concurrency control (MVCC), and a crash-safe write-ahead log.
verification: Deterministic integration suite feeding malformed JSON documents, concurrent transaction rollbacks, and simulated disk corruption to verify atomic recovery.
major_features: Custom query parser supporting JSON-path filtering and projection operators
B+Tree on-disk index manager with fixed-size node splitting and merging
Multi-Version Concurrency Control (MVCC) snapshot isolation for readers and writers
Binary Write-Ahead Log (WAL) with CRC32 checksums for transactional durability
Slotted-page storage allocator supporting variable-length document packing
Background checkpointing daemon to flush dirty cache pages and prune old WAL segments
Virtual Thread-based concurrent transaction coordinator handling lock escalation
Crash-recovery engine replaying transaction logs to restore consistent state
truth_policy: Only validated behavior may be claimed as working.
